market_implied_expectations: Reverse-DCF (valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md — same WACC 9.20%, terminal growth 3.5%, 10-year horizon, mid-year discounting as the run's own intrinsic-dcf, 04): at $68.18 the market is pricing in only a 5.05% constant annual FCFF growth rate over 10 years, roughly 1.5 years of above-GDP growth before the model must fall to the 3.5% terminal rate, and a 10.78% steady-state EBIT margin. All three read as conservative: the implied FCFF CAGR sits below both Uber's own FY2023-2025 revenue CAGR (18.1%) and the run's own DCF base case (04, 6.54% 10-yr FCFF CAGR); the implied ~1.5 years of above-GDP growth is a small fraction of 04's own assumed 10 years; and the implied 10.78% steady-state margin is already below Uber's actual trailing 12-month EBIT margin (12.13%, TTM through Jun-30-2026) and well below the Q2 FY26 quarterly margin (~13.3%). Robustness: the FCF-base definition, not the discount rate, is the dominant sensitivity (implied CAGR ranges 3.35%-10.02% across three defensible base-year definitions vs. 2.63%-7.21% across a WACC ±1pp band); terminal-g sensitivity is smaller still (4.29%-5.74%). [valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md §2-4]
engine_view: Base-case fair value $74.77/share (+9.67% above the $68.18 price), bull $104.17 (+52.79%, 12mo), bear_cyclical $47.24 (-30.71%, 12mo), bear_structural $43.38 (-36.37%, 24-36mo AV-disruption floor) [valuation/07_scenario-and-fair-value.md; valuation/99_valuation-synthesis.md]. The dominant method (peer-relative NTM EV/EBITDA, 38% weight) converges within 1.2% of an independent own-history-multiple check, and the intrinsic DCF (04) independently implies a 6.54% 10-year FCFF CAGR base case — above the 5.05% the price requires. But the published base case prices in NEITHER of the two Critical governance red flags: the unresolved federal derivative lawsuit naming the CEO, Chairman, and full board (RF-MGT-005) nor the pending $14.8bn debt-funded Delivery Hero acquisition (RF-CAP-004) — both are explicitly absent from every fair-value level in valuation/99, meaning the true risk-adjusted engine view is arguably lower than $74.77, not higher [final_thesis.md §6]. The synthesizer's own probability-weighted scenario math nets to an expected return of only +1.57%, a 36.37% downside risk, and a 0.05 risk/reward — the run's own conclusion is that this does not reward initiating a position even though the base-case point estimate sits modestly above the current price. Final decision: Watchlist, no position, capped by the two Critical red flags independent of the valuation read.
what_everyone_knows: Uber is the largest, most profitable ride-hailing/delivery platform, growing Gross Bookings above 20% (constant currency) for four straight quarters, and is buying Delivery Hero in the biggest deal in its history.
what_is_priced_in: A slowing, not accelerating, growth story: the market prices just a 5.05% ten-year free-cash-flow growth rate (reverse-DCF) and a 10.78% steady-state margin Uber has already beaten on a trailing basis (12.13% TTM EBIT margin); revenue consensus has also been cut 1.04% in the three trading days after the Q2 print.
what_market_may_be_missing: Two things pulling in opposite directions: (1) the reported revenue deceleration (18%->12.2% YoY) is substantially a one-time UK accounting reclassification (~$1.1bn/quarter), not weaker demand, and the market may be under-crediting genuine ~20-25% underlying growth; (2) at the same time, the 4-quarter EBITDA guidance-beat streak the market implicitly trusts likely still nets a recurring 'one-off' legal-reserve add-back (17.3% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2024, 6.5% in FY2025) that the company stopped reconciling to GAAP starting Q1 FY2026 -- a real earnings-quality gap the beat-streak narrative does not price.
evidence_engine_is_different: Cited, quantified, filing-anchored evidence on both halves of the divergence, not just a differing opinion: the UK VAT/business-model reclassification's $1.1bn/quarter revenue impact is disclosed and reconciled [earnings/01, business-model/10]; the ex-UK cost-of-revenue ratio improved +377bps in Q2 FY26 alone -- larger than the entire quarter's net EBITDA-margin gain [earnings/03]; the reverse-DCF's implied 5.05% FCFF growth and 10.78% margin are solved from the identical model (WACC, terminal g, horizon) as the run's own intrinsic DCF, and both sit below already-delivered TTM actuals [valuation/05 §2-3]. On the offsetting side, the 17.3%/6.5% recurring 'non-recurring' legal-reserve add-back and the Q1 FY2026 discontinuation of the Adjusted-EBITDA-to-GAAP reconciliation are both filing-cited [management-governance/06, business-model/12 (RF-RFS-001, RF-DISC-001, RF-DISC-002)].
base_rate_check: Passes on the growth/margin axis: betting Uber merely sustains already-delivered results (18.1% FY2023-2025 revenue CAGR, 12.13% TTM EBIT margin, a 4-for-4 EBITDA guidance-beat streak) is not an exceptional forecast against those metrics' own recent history -- the reverse-DCF hurdle (5.05% FCFF growth, 10.78% margin) sits below both, so this is a conservative, not an exceptional, forecast. Fails, or at least cuts the other way, on the M&A/moat axis used to judge the offsetting risk: Uber's own serial-acquirer base rate (Drizly -- $1.1bn full write-off within 2.5 years; Careem sold to a minority stake then re-bought to control) argues the pending $14.8bn Delivery Hero deal should be judged skeptically against that base rate, not credited as upside: and the 5-year through-cycle ROIC of only +0.85% (vs. an estimated ~9.7% WACC) is the more relevant longer-run base rate for whether Uber's economics durably clear its cost of capital, versus extrapolating the last 1-2 years (ROIC above WACC) forward without qualification [final_thesis.md §4, §9A; business-model/09_moat.md; management-governance/02].
